excludedForConflictingAnswerKeys.feedback: Under PSR Rule 120224(b), the MDA must certify that the staff member can be released to undertake Sabbatical Leave without replacement or impairing the smooth flow of work.
excludedForConflictingAnswerKeys.question: The Officer’s MDA must certify what before Sabbatical Leave is granted?
options: That the Officer can be released without replacement or impairing the smooth flow of work
That the Officer must be dismissed first
That the Officer is no longer needed in Service
That the Officer will not return
excludedForConflictingAnswerKeys.answer: That the Officer can be released without replacement or impairing the smooth flow of work

scenarioSources.scenario: Your annual leave dates are pencilled into your diary, but your superior has not authorized your absence. A colleague urges you to travel tonight.
Your unit needs cover throughout the year. You propose splitting your annual leave into four separate blocks.
You have approved annual leave and intend to spend it abroad. Your itinerary and overseas address are ready.
While on vacation leave, you are formally required to perform official duty for several days. The leave ledger still counts those days as holiday.
Your leave was curtailed for an official assignment. The assignment is now complete and a colleague suggests saving the balance for several years.
You wake up too ill to attend work. Your supervisor is expecting you, but no notification has been sent.
You obtain medical treatment while away from your usual duty location. You have not yet told your employer.
An officer is so ill that they cannot visit the health provider. You are the next of kin assisting them.
An officer remains unfit for duty after three months of certified illness. The file reaches your desk for the next step.
A Medical Board has issued recommendations that differ from the earlier advice of the health provider. You must process the case.
A professional recruit needs additional qualifying experience before appointment in the full grade. You are preparing the appointment paperwork.
A trainee has satisfactorily completed the prescribed training. Your unit must prepare the next appointment action.
An already confirmed officer is appointed to a training grade. HR asks how to treat the officer during training.
A proposed training secondment would extend beyond the normal training period. You are asked to process it as routine.
A confirmed officer in a lower post has been converted to a higher post. A draft letter places the officer on probation again solely because of that conversion.
You are a newly appointed professional officer covered by the compulsory confirmation examination requirement. There is no Government exemption, and you are planning your development timetable.
A direct appointee covered by the confirmation examination rule has served only three months and asks HR to register them immediately.
An officer is promoted from an unconfirmed junior post into a covered professional grade. The officer believes promotion alone removes the confirmation examination requirement.
An officer transfers from another Scheduled Service at age 35 and has not satisfied confirmation conditions. You review the examination requirement.
An officer is preparing for further advancement beyond GL. 10. A colleague suggests an attendance slip from any unapproved social seminar will suffice.
